standard_prerequisites.name: I-power torsion submodules and the quotient by the torsion submodule
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the reduction that removes the torsion part and leaves a torsion-free quotient to control.

standard_prerequisites.name: The adjoint tensor-restrict isomorphism for a base change of rings
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the Hom isomorphism in the case where the target module is already I-power torsion.

standard_prerequisites.name: The neighbourhood isomorphism lemma identifying modules with their base change when annihilated by a power of I
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets M[I^∞] and its base change be identified, and later lets N be replaced by N[I^∞].

standard_prerequisites.name: The divide-by-torsion lemma producing a module with no I-power torsion
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies M'[I^∞] = 0, which makes the map into the direct sum of t copies injective.

core_obligations: Record that the equivalent conditions of the flatness-on-torsion and neighbourhood-isomorphism lemmas are satisfied and will be used without further mention (proof lines 24321-24324).

Part (1): for arbitrary M set M' = M/M[I^∞], use the exact sequence 0 -> M[I^∞] -> M -> M' -> 0 and M[I^∞] = M[I^∞] tensor_R S to reduce to showing (M' tensor_R S)[(IS)^∞] = 0 (proof lines 24325-24331).

Part (1), conclusion: write I = (f_1, ..., f_t), use the divide-by-torsion lemma to get M'[I^∞] = 0, so that x -> (f_1^n x, ..., f_t^n x) into the direct sum of t copies of M' is injective for every n > 0; by flatness of S the base-changed map is also injective, which says (M' tensor_R S)[I^n] = 0 (proof lines 24332-24342).
Part (2), first case: if N is I-power torsion then N tensor_R S = N and the displayed map is an isomorphism by the adjoint tensor-restrict lemma (proof lines 24345-24347).

Part (2), second case: if M is I-power torsion, the image of any M -> N factors through N[I^∞] and the image of any base-changed map factors through (N tensor_R S)[(IS)^∞], so part (1) lets one replace N by N[I^∞] and reduce to the previous case (proof lines 24348-24354).

Part (3): conclude that the base change functor is fully faithful from (2), and establish essential surjectivity by checking directly that an IS-power torsion module is the base change of an I-power torsion module (proof lines 24357-24358 and following).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a flat ring map R -> S and a finitely generated ideal I with R/I -> S/IS an isomorphism, and asserts three things: that the natural map on I-power torsion submodules is an isomorphism; that Hom_R(M, N) -> Hom_S(M tensor_R S, N tensor_R S) is an isomorphism whenever either M or N is I-power torsion; and that base change is an equivalence between I-power torsion modules and IS-power torsion modules (source lines 24300-24318). The proof gives each part. Part (1) sets M' = M/M[I^∞] and uses the exact sequence 0 -> M[I^∞] -> M -> M' -> 0 together with M[I^∞] = M[I^∞] tensor_R S to reduce to showing (M' tensor_R S)[(IS)^∞] = 0; writing I = (f_1, ..., f_t), it uses the divide-by-torsion lemma to get M'[I^∞] = 0, so the map x -> (f_1^n x, ..., f_t^n x) into the direct sum of t copies of M' is injective for every n > 0, and flatness of S keeps it injective after base change, giving (M' tensor_R S)[I^n] = 0 as required (proof lines 24325-24342). Part (2) splits into two cases: if N is I-power torsion then N tensor_R S = N and the map is an isomorphism by the adjoint tensor-restrict lemma; if M is I-power torsion then any map M -> N lands in N[I^∞] and any map after base change lands in (N tensor_R S)[(IS)^∞], so part (1) lets one replace N by N[I^∞] and reduce to the previous case (proof lines 24345-24354). Part (3) argues that the functor is fully faithful by (2) and checks essential surjectivity for IS-power torsion modules (proof lines 24357-24358 and following). The non-routine steps are the injection-into-a-direct-sum argument in part (1) and the reduction of part (2) to the case already handled.
